terms.definition: A pattern in which measured values or categories of two variables differ together in a sampled dataset; the pattern alone does not specify why it occurs. Every measure in this lesson quantifies how large such a pattern is, and none of them turns it into a cause.

alignment.note: Adopts the meaning established by PREM-SCI-007: a pattern in which two variables differ together in a sample, with no claim about why. This lesson adds only measurement, giving the pattern a size through the risk difference, risk ratio, and odds ratio, and repeats that the size of an association says nothing about its cause.

terms.definition: The probability that a stated outcome occurs in a stated group over a stated period, written as a share of that group. It is a conditional probability with the group named in the condition, and it carries no verdict about harm: a risk of recovery is a risk in this sense. The everyday sense of danger is a different meaning of the word.

The risk of the outcome in the group that did not receive the intervention, or in the comparison group of an observed contrast. It is the starting point a relative measure divides out and an absolute measure preserves, which is why the same relative change corresponds to different numbers of people at different baselines.

One group's risk subtracted from the other's. It is an absolute measure: it keeps the units of the outcome, so it states how many people per hundred, or per thousand, the comparison moves. When the comparison is an intervention that lowers risk it is usually called the absolute risk reduction.

One group's risk divided by the other's. It is a relative measure: the units cancel, so it states how many times as large one risk is and says nothing about where either started. One minus the ratio is the relative risk reduction.

The probability that an event occurs divided by the probability that it does not, which counting people is cases per non-case. Odds and risk carry the same information and convert freely, by odds = risk / (1 - risk) and risk = odds / (1 + odds). The betting sense of the word contributes only the cases-to-non-cases form, and nothing about stakes or payouts.

The odds in one group divided by the odds in the other, equal to the cross-product of the diagonals of a two-by-two table of counts. It approximates the risk ratio when the outcome is rare and sits further from 1 than the risk ratio when the outcome is common, so it may not be read as a risk ratio without checking how often the outcome occurred.

The reciprocal of the risk difference: the number of people who would have to receive one condition instead of the other, over a stated period, for one additional person to change outcome. It is meaningless without its time period, its comparison, and the baseline risk it was computed from. Pointed at an unwanted outcome, the same arithmetic is called a number needed to harm.

The proportion of a defined population with a specified condition or characteristic at a stated time or over a stated period. In this lesson it is the share of a tested group whose reference standard says the target condition is present, and it is the quantity that moves a test's predictive values without touching its sensitivity or specificity.

alignment.note: Adopts the definition established by PREM-SCI-004 without change: the proportion of a defined population with a specified condition at a stated time. This lesson applies that meaning to the group a test is used in, and shows that it is what separates a test's detection measures from its predictive values.

terms.definition: The procedure treated as giving the correct answer while a test is being judged against it. It is the best available comparison for the study at hand and not a guarantee of truth, so a test's reported figures describe its agreement with that particular standard.

Among people who have the target condition according to the reference standard, the share whose test is positive: P(test positive given condition present). It divides the true positives by a group defined by the reference standard, so it describes the test. The everyday sense of being easily affected is unrelated, and so is the sensitivity analysis of PREM-SCI-009 and PREM-SCI-010, which reruns a result under different assumptions.

Among people who do not have the target condition according to the reference standard, the share whose test is negative: P(test negative given condition absent). It divides the true negatives by a group defined by the reference standard, so it too describes the test. Its complement is the false-positive rate.

Among people whose test was positive, the share who have the target condition: P(condition present given test positive). It divides the true positives by a group defined by the test result, so it describes the person holding that result, and it falls as the condition becomes less common in the group tested. Note that a positive result means the test fired, which for most tests is unwelcome news.

Among people whose test was negative, the share who do not have the target condition: P(condition absent given test negative). It divides the true negatives by a group defined by the test result, and it rises as the condition becomes less common in the group tested, moving opposite to the positive predictive value.
